title: CityReportBoard
description: The API provides two endpoints for a city-based report board. Users submit a report with a location string and receive an authentication token and a report identifier. The location is parsed to determine the city using a comma-based rule: the last comma‑separated segment is taken as the city (whitespace trimmed). Users can later retrieve a list of reports limited to their own city by supplying the authentication token. Reports include a public profile identifier for the author, content, and city.
declared_purpose: To allow users to share reports with other users registered in the same city.
allowed_data_use: Process the location to extract city; display reports only to authenticated users whose city matches the report’s city; use email internally for account management; author identification via public profile_id.
forbidden_data_use: Must not expose email or precise location to any user; must not return reports when the requester’s city does not match the report’s city.
allowed_storage: Email (for account management), extracted city, report content, public profile_id, and authentication token may be stored persistently. Resource content and access-control rules (city ownership) may be stored.
forbidden_storage: Exact latitude, longitude, GPS coordinates, street address, full address, and the original location string must not be stored, returned, retained, or exposed.
expected_privacy_preserving_behavior: API responses contain no email or precise location. GET /reports only returns reports whose city matches the authenticated user’s city. The database does not contain any original location string or precise address; only the extracted city is stored. The public profile_id is not an email.
expected_privacy_violating_behavior: Email or precise location appears in an API response. The database contains an original location string or full address. GET /reports returns reports from other cities. Unauthenticated requests successfully list reports.
schema:
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: CityReportBoard
  description: API for submitting city-based reports and retrieving reports by city using an authentication token.
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /reports:
    post:
      summary: Submit a new report
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                location:
                  type: string
                  description: A location string; the city is extracted as the last comma-separated segment (whitespace trimmed).
                  example: "123 Main St, Springfield, IL"
                content:
                  type: string
                  description: The report content.
                  example: "Pothole on Main Street"
                profile_id:
                  type: string
                  description: Public identifier for the author.
                  example: "user123"
              required:
                - location
                - content
                - profile_id
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Report submitted successfully.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  token:
                    type: string
                    description: Authentication token that grants access to reports from the same city.
                    example: "abc123citytoken"
                  report_id:
                    type: string
                    description: Unique identifier for the submitted report.
                    example: "rep-456"
        '400':
          description: Invalid input.
    get:
      summary: Retrieve reports for the city associated with the provided token
      parameters:
        - in: query
          name: token
          schema:
            type: string
          required: true
          description: Authentication token obtained from a previous report submission.
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A list of reports for the city.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    report_id:
                      type: string
                      example: "rep-456"
                    profile_id:
                      type: string
                      example: "user123"
                    content:
                      type: string
                      example: "Pothole on Main Street"
                    city:
                      type: string
                      example: "IL"
        '400':
          description: Invalid or missing token.
        '401':
          description: Invalid token.
text_spec:
The server, named CityReportBoard, provides two endpoints for submitting and retrieving city-based reports. The first endpoint, accessible via POST /reports, allows users to submit a new report. The request body must be a JSON object containing three required fields: "location" (a string describing the location), "content" (the report text), and "profile_id" (a public identifier for the author). The server extracts the city from the location string by taking the last comma-separated segment and trimming whitespace. Upon successful submission, the server responds with status 201 and a JSON object containing two fields: "token", an authentication token that grants access to reports from the same city, and "report_id", a unique identifier for the submitted report. If the input is invalid, a 400 status is returned.

The second endpoint, accessible via GET /reports, retrieves all reports associated with the city linked to a given authentication token. The request must include a query parameter "token" containing the token obtained from a previous report submission. The server responds with status 200 and a JSON array of report objects. Each object includes "report_id", "profile_id", "content", and "city" (the extracted city string). If the token is missing or invalid, the server returns a 400 status; if the token is invalid (e.g., not recognized), a 401 status is returned.
